questions.question: The Bhotia dance form is a folk-dance from which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution: The Bhotia dance is a traditional folk dance of the Uttarakhand Himalayas, performed by the Bhotia community. It is often linked to soul-migration rituals (Dhurang) and is characterized by dancers holding white handkerchiefs while moving in a circular pattern.

questions.question: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form of:
questions.solution: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form from Kerala. Known as the 'Dance of the Enchantress,' it is performed solo by women and features graceful, swaying movements and white-and-gold costumes (Kasavu).

questions.question: Rouf is the traditional dance of __________, which is practiced on the festive occasions of Eid and during Ramzan days.
questions.solution: Rouf is the most popular traditional dance of Jammu & Kashmir. It is primarily performed by women during the spring season and major festivals like Eid, involving two rows of dancers facing each other and performing intricate footwork while singing folk lyrics.

questions.question: Rukmini Devi Arundale is associated with which are form?
questions.solution: Rukmini Devi Arundale was a transformative figure in the world of Dance. She is credited with the 'renaissance' of Bharatanatyam, stripping it of its social stigma and establishing the Kalakshetra Foundation in Chennai.

questions.question: Bharatanatyam dance form is associated with:
questions.solution: Bharatanatyam is the oldest classical dance tradition of India, originating from the temples of Tamil Nadu. It was formerly known as Sadir Attam and is celebrated for its precise footwork and sophisticated sign language (Mudras).

questions.question: Kalbelia dance, also known as the 'Sapera Dance', is the folk dance of ________.
questions.solution: Kalbelia is a vibrant folk dance of Rajasthan, performed by the tribe of the same name. Also known as the 'Sapera Dance', its movements and swirling black costumes are designed to mimic the flexibility and grace of a cobra.

questions.question: Balasaraswati who was regarded as child prodigy by Vidhwans and Pandits played an important role in reviving the dance form ______________.
questions.solution: T. Balasaraswati was a legendary Bharatanatyam dancer who belonged to a traditional family of temple musicians and dancers. Regarded as a child prodigy, she was instrumental in gaining international recognition for the dance form.

questions.question:
With reference to 'Saila dance' consider the following statements and select the correct option.

a) A group comprising of male performers.

b) The dance is performed with bamboo sticks.

c) It is performed after the cutting of crops.
questions.solution: All three statements about the Saila dance are correct. It is a popular folk dance in Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh performed by male dancers using sticks to celebrate a successful harvest season.

questions.question: Which is the only surviving specimen of the ancient Sanskrit theatre recognised by UNESCO as a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity?
questions.solution: Kutiyattam (Koodiyattam) from Kerala is the only surviving specimen of ancient Sanskrit theatre. It is over 2,000 years old and was the first Indian art form to be recognized by UNESCO as a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity.

questions.question: Who is the author of Natyashashtra?
questions.solution: Bharata Muni is the legendary author of the Natyashastra, the foundational ancient treatise on the performing arts, including dance, music, and drama. It is often referred to as the 'Fifth Veda'.
